subject: AI & Agents
title: Batch Size, Epochs, and Learning Rate
description: A 1-minute de-risking session on Batch Size, Epochs, and Learning Rate.

hook.text: Three numbers control how a model trains: how much data per step, how many passes, how fast to learn.

buildup.text: Batch size = examples per gradient update. Epoch = one full pass through data. Learning rate = step size.

discovery.text: Small batches add noise that can help escape bad solutions. Large batches are more stable.

twist.text: The learning rate is the most critical setting. Too high: divergence. Too low: no progress.

climax.text: Modern training uses learning rate schedules that start high and decay over time.

punchline.text: Training is a balancing act of speed, stability, and patience.

quiz.question: What happens if the learning rate is too high?
options: The model overshoots good solutions and diverges
Training becomes slower but more accurate

details.summary: Batch size, epochs, and learning rate are key training hyperparameters. Batch size controls examples per update, epochs control passes through data, and learning rate controls step size during optimization.
details.whyItMatters: Tuning these hyperparameters determines whether training succeeds. Wrong settings cause models to diverge, overfit, or waste compute. Understanding them is essential for practical ML.
takeaways: Batch size sets how many examples are processed per weight update
Epochs count complete passes through the entire training dataset
Learning rate controls how much weights change each step

faq.question: What happens if the learning rate is too high or too low?
faq.answer: Too high and the model overshoots optimal values, diverging or oscillating wildly. Too low and training takes forever or gets stuck in suboptimal solutions. Finding the right rate is crucial for successful training.

faq.question: How do practitioners choose the right hyperparameters?
faq.answer: Through systematic experimentation: grid search, random search, or automated methods like Bayesian optimization. Learning rate schedulers that adjust the rate during training are also common practice.
